title: Shared compression library: correctness passed, timing unresolved
headline: The full correctness matrix passed. The first baseline timing guest failed decode observation, leaving performance unmeasured.

sections.title: Separate reusable mechanism from frontend policy
sections.lead: The experiment extracts codec contexts and compressed-object storage from ZSwap. Existing policy, indexes, accounting and lifetime ownership stay with the frontend. This is the first step toward independent XSwap and later tier migration.

blocks.text: The full correctness matrix passed. The first baseline timing guest failed decode observation, leaving performance unmeasured.
R5 collected eight fresh correctness guests and two disabled-configuration builds before timing. All required correctness rows passed; its subsequent baseline measurement failed.

sections.title: 1. Whole system: restore the application page
sections.lead: An application needs its full page in physical RAM. Stored contents may be compressed inside RAM or reside on a backing device. Compression trades CPU work for less storage traffic.

blocks.takeaway: The changed engine serves compressed contents inside RAM
blocks.note: Schematic path, with no illustrative size or timing used as a measurement.

blocks.text: The candidate changes the compressed-storage implementation. The existing frontend still decides admission, accounting and writeback. No new RAM-to-disk migration policy is implemented here.

sections.title: 2. Subsystem: policy keeps the object identity
sections.lead: ZSwap retains the entry index, memory-group charge, ordering and lifetime pins. A shared page library owns per-CPU codec contexts, scratch buffers and compressed-object storage.

blocks.takeaway: Data moves through the engine; policy stays with the frontend

blocks.text: The unchanged ownership boundary passed exact-source review. R5 subsequently passed complete required correctness, including NUMA placement, guest CPU hotplug, legacy behavior and accounting.

sections.title: 3. Concrete change: one object engine, the same frontend owner
sections.lead: Before extraction, ZSwap owns both policy and the codec/object engine. After extraction, the library returns a handle and length while ZSwap keeps publication, charges, LRU and references. Each stored object retains its original representation.

blocks.takeaway: Move the reusable engine behind an explicit ownership boundary

blocks.text: The review found no per-object wrapper or context-size increase. Extraction adds a pool allocation and a small requested pool-size increase; allocator rounding is unmeasured. New API and test obligations remain.

sections.title: Proceed to independent XSwap with fresh measurement evidence
sections.lead: Keep original A as the comparison anchor. C2 must demonstrate actual compressed objects, decoder calls, generic objcg charges and balanced teardown with ZSWAP disabled. Its prospective observer isolation is applied to both arms and needs fresh calibration.

blocks.takeaway: Functional dependency passes; performance remains a separate gate

blocks.text: Source identities and saved correctness have high confidence. The timing cause remains unresolved: R6 collected no trace. No performance winner, baseline advancement or code promotion exists. C2/C3 execution still requires its own gates.
